title: EU seeks nominations for stakeholder group on tokenisation standards in finance
summary: EU seeks nominations for stakeholder group on tokenisation standards in finance 09 November 2026 Digital Finance and Innovation The European Central Bank (ECB), together with the European Commission and the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA), is calling upon wholesale financial industry stakeholders to express their interest in joining the European Tokenisation Standards Group (ETSG). The group will bring together industry stakeholders to develop common standards for an interconnected tokenised financial ecosystem. The group aims to establish a framework for monitoring compliance with the agreed standards and may formulate recommendations for EU authorities on how to incentivise compliance with those standards. Its work will be market-driven and shaped by the contributions and consensus of industry stakeholders. To this end, the ETSG will be chaired by participants from the industry, with the ECB, the Commission and ESMA acting as observers. Participation in the ETSG is open to a wide range of stakeholders, including EU associations, private entities, global institutions, fintech companies and technical providers working on tokenisation or DLT-based financial services

title: The EBA streamlines the 2027 EU-wide stress test with more than 55% reduction in requested data
summary: The European Banking Authority (EBA) today released the final methodology, draft templates, and template guidance for its 2027 EU-wide stress test, together with the key milestones for the exercise. Following extensive engagement with industry participants, the EBA has significantly streamlined the exercise, reducing the number of required data points by 55% through the simplification of reporting templates and closer alignment with supervisory reporting. These changes will reduce operational burden and improve efficiency while preserving the robustness, risk-sensitivity and comparability of stress test results. The 2027 exercise will also include, for the first time, a dedicated module assessing climate-related risks. The 2027 EU-wide stress test will formally start in January 2027, following the release of the macroeconomic and climate scenarios, with the results scheduled for publication by the end of July 2027.

title: The EBA publishes consumer factsheet on white-labelled financial products and services
summary: The European Banking Authority (EBA) published today a factsheet to help consumers identify when a banking or payment product or service is white labelled, i.e. marketed under one brand but provided by another company. As consumers increasingly access financial products and services through online platforms, retailers and other non-financial brands, it may be sometimes unclear which company is responsible for providing the product or service. Understanding this distinction can help consumers make informed decisions, know who they are dealing with and reduce risks. For this reason, the factsheet also guides consumers on the key things to know and check before getting that product or service.
